provenance.note: Every row below was produced by a real request. Anything not listed here is deliberately unmatched and resolves to endpoint_unavailable.

headers.Content-Type: <the media type, which must match the file extension>

wire.observedNote: Single phase. There is no policy call and no second host. A request with no body answers 400 Invalid Content-Type, so the Content-Type header is what carries the declared type.

rows.observed: Returned identically for: a wrong repository_id, a repository we can read but cannot push to (cli/cli), and an omitted repository_id.
rows.why: Three different causes produce a byte-identical response. Naming one of them would be a guess presented as a diagnosis.

bodySignals: content_type is not included in the list of allowed content types
name has a file extension that does not match the content type
rows.observed: Both messages can arrive in the SAME response, in errors[]. A .log declared as text/plain produced the first alone; a .png declared as application/octet-stream produced both.
rows.why: A body can carry more than one reason at once, so the message must be disjunctive rather than picking whichever matched first.

rows.observed: Sent with no body and no Content-Type header.

default.why: Anything not matched above leaves the state of the remote side unknown. Uploads cannot be withdrawn, so an unrecognised answer is never guessed at and never retried.

unresolvedUnknowns: Abuse detection and rate limiting were not observed. A matrix of this size cannot trigger them, so a 403 with an HTML body remains possible and unclassified — it would resolve to endpoint_unavailable, which is the safe direction.
Behaviour with an installation token (ghs_) was not tested; CI is out of scope and GITHUB_TOKEN is deliberately never read.
A classic PAT without the repo scope was not tested — that credential has to be issued by hand.
Behaviour when the connection drops after the body has been sent was not induced deliberately; the transport treats it as request-started, which is the conservative reading.
Video types (.mp4, .webm, .mov) and the size ceiling were not probed: each success would have cost another permanent asset, and the image cases already establish the accept/reject shape.
